Hi Alex — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

1) High-level SLOs you asked about (95th perc):
   - Small inputs (<=512 tokens total): target <= 250ms
   - Medium inputs (~2k tokens): target <= 500ms
   - Large context (16k input + up to 2k output): target asymmetric — on encode/first-token we expect higher cost; you indicated an upper bound of ~1.2s for first-token across the worst-case scenario

2) Throughput/concurrency:
   - Typical concurrency target: 50-100 concurrent requests for peak periods; burst headroom to 200 for short spikes
   - Target sustained QPS: ~80

3) Streaming requirements:
   - You need streaming partial tokens to the client within 100ms of generation start for long outputs (so UI can show live responses).

4) Context window clarification:
   - You clarified calls will include long historical context (customer chat transcripts + metadata) up to ~16k tokens on some requests, with typical average closer to 4–6k tokens. Output size usually <2k tokens.

5) Latency expectations & notes from our side:
   - Encoding a 16k context will add measurable upfront time: prompt encoding and KV cache priming are proportional to context length. For optimized kernels and continuous KV cache the added cost is roughly linear in context length for the encoder pass, but generation throughput per token is similar to shorter contexts once priming is done.
   - For streaming-first-token SLAs we recommend a configuration that prioritizes low tail latency (smaller batch windows for streaming requests + dedicated capacity).

Attachments: FinCo_latency_matrix_v2.xlsx (latency-by-context-size & concurrency scenarios), redwood_slo_playbook.pdf (recommended configs & tradeoffs).

Next steps I propose:
- Connor: run baseline perf runs for the 3 representative scenarios (512 tokens, 2k tokens, 16k context + 1k output) on our recommended config and share numbers by end of week.
- We’ll draft a 2-week POC proposal that includes streaming validation and throughput/latency dashboards.
- Procurement/Legal: if you want, loop in procurement so we can align on timing for Dedicated capacity pricing.

Are we aligned? If anything above is off, call it out and I’ll update.

Thanks,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — that recap is really helpful and matches our notes. A few clarifications/questions: 

- The 1.2s for first-token on 16k context is an upper bound we can tolerate; lower is better. For streaming we care most about first-token and steady delivery of subsequent token groups (we typically render every ~100 tokens).
- For concurrency: the 50–100 sustained is accurate; spikes to 200 are realistic around certain scheduled events.
- Can you confirm whether the recommended config supports vertical scaling (bigger GPU) vs horizontal (more smaller nodes)? We're flexible but want to understand cost/latency tradeoffs.
